claims.text: The GPS trace measures this trip at 27.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a platform optimal of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.43% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal (4.2 km) and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own measurement, and I rely on the governing trace figure rather than the rounded trip_record copy.

The driver admitted the detour in the in-app chat at 10:42:05 — 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now' — and repeated that admission in his own counterparty statement ('I took a wrong turn at the MCE exit and had to come back around'). A driver admission in the chat_log is itself an independent corroborating source named in POL-RD-07, and here it confirms the deviation without any need to lean on the trace alone.

No advisory covers the AYE/MCE/ECP corridor in the 10:14-10:59 window on 12 July 2026: the artifact EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0. With no traffic_advisory naming the affected segment, POL-RD-03 exoneration cannot run, and nothing on this record excuses the excess as an external closure or contraflow.

The chat log records no rider instruction to detour. The only rider messages are a question ('why we going towards city centre? MBS is the other side') and a bare 'ok'. No waypoint_hint is set on any message and no road is named, so the corroboration test for POL-RD-04 is not met and the clause is unavailable; the driver's own words attribute the detour to his missed exit, not to anything the rider asked for.

POL-RD-05 does not apply. Both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no endpoint was relocated and the booked optimal of 21.0 km stands as the baseline against which the excess is measured.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 burden. Trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-00101, and the trace's first fix (10:21:05) matches the recorded start; the 6.18 km excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace (100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s, no jump over 500 m). The burden therefore shifts to the driver to invoke a specific exculpatory clause, and he has pointed to none — he has admitted the missed exit instead.

The rider carries no adverse claim pattern. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4 in POL-RD-08, so the enhanced corroboration rule for low-substantiation riders does not apply and the claim is proven on the trace plus the driver's admission alone.

Under POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. The fare model is METERED and recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. The charged total is 35.64, so the refund is 35.64 - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 as 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and is 22.5% of the charged total, well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the rider is owed a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05.

No off-route ERP or tolls complicate the correction: erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is 0.00, so the entire difference sits in the distance and time charges that POL-RD-02 already corrects. There is no third-party pass-through line to net against the rider's refund.

Every artifact the rider's case rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown all carry no admissibility issues — so under POL-GEN-02 there is no impairment discount on the deciding facts, and the only zero-weight artifact is the advisory whose absence itself supports this claim.

Both parties are substantially in agreement on the arithmetic, and the record supports it.

The deviation is ESTABLISHED. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 27.18 km (EV-GPS-00101), not the rounded trip_record copy of 27.2 km; the platform optimal is 21.0 km (EV-TRIP-00101). Excess = 6.18 km, or 29.43% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km). The excess is NOT material: it is below 50% of optimal and below 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile uplift and conduct referral are not engaged. I have checked the driver profile anyway — deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 812, a ratio of 0.00 — so no pattern exists even on the clause's own test. I confirm that driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags (lifetime) is a near-synonym of the trailing counter POL-RD-06 names and, per POL-GEN-01, is context only; the driver advocate correctly declined to use it, and I place no weight on it either.

The driver's own words carry the finding independently of the trace: in the in-app chat at 10:42:05 he wrote 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now' (EV-CHAT-00101), and his counterparty statement repeats it. That is an admission against his own interest and would support the finding even if the trace were removed. The trace is in any case unimpaired — 229 fixes, 100% coverage, max gap 0.0 s, no jump over 500 m — so no POL-RD-07 consequences arise and no independent corroboration was required. No exculpatory clause applies: there is no traffic_advisory in the pool (EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), the rider gave no instruction or waypoint (waypoint_hint is null on every message, so POL-RD-04 cannot run), and no pickup or dropoff was amended (both amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply).

The money is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 21.0 + 0.28 × 26.0) × 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. charged_total = 35.64. Refund = 35.64 − 27.63 = 8.01, which is not below the 0.50 de minimis floor, and rounded UP to SGD 8.05. At 8.05 the refund is 22.47% of charged_total, far short of the 90% that would promote it to a FULL_REFUND. There are no ERP, toll, airport-surcharge or waiting-time lines (all 0.00, erp_gantries empty), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top and nothing is netted off. The rider's contested figure of 10.00 is not supported by the fare model; the correct figure is 8.05.

No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trace is unimpaired, trip identifiers match, no admissible evidence conflicts, no unmatched charge line exists, and my confidence is above the 0.70 floor. On confidence: every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the GPS trace, the trip record and the chat log — sits at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0. The MISSING advisory (weight 0.0) carries no fact; its absence is simply citable, and since no party relied on a closure it changes nothing.

No referral is produced. POL-RD-06(c) requires an established repeat pattern (there is none), and POL-RD-09(4) requires an unmatched or phantom charge line (there is none). Accordingly the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.05 to the rider, with no driver compensation (the billed distance is not less than the traced distance, so POL-RD-04's shortfall limb does not arise).
